analysis:
All supplied changes are test-only. In EngineV2BridgeTests.swift the changes add a decodeTable to the stub tokenizer, a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge helper, and scoped stop-sequence tests (the new patch lines are 811-896). The visible head excerpts (lines 2448-3217) cover prefix-cache receipt lookup outcomes, an L1/L2 resident-versus-SSD preflight test, seeded-id and receipt isolation tests, logprobs channel capping, and paged KV capacity tests. In EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift the only change is line 313, which adds `.logprobs` to the ignored cases in a switch over MLXServerGenerationEvent. That keeps the test helper exhaustive and has no production effect. No production source, authorization, attestation, encryption, or network-facing behavior changed in this batch.

Relevant threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache). The tests use temporary directories, random SymmetricKey KEKs, and fixed cache scopes. They exercise the existing SSDPrefixCache API, HMAC-tagged lookup, corrupt-file rejection (missCorrupt), no-I/O behavior for equal or shorter SSD matches, and per-scope receipt isolation. They do not weaken any control. They write fake 100-byte files into the test store and expect corruption detection, which reinforces the fail-closed behavior in the threat model. Nothing here changes the TTL, the disk-budget policy, the name derivation, or the AAD.

Open question for integration: the production changes behind these test updates are not in this batch. These are the stop-string scoping in EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence and ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, the new .logprobs event, and the receipt and preflight tier ordering. They should be reviewed in their own source units. The tests only indicate intended behavior.
